resources.string: What Prune can do on this device

Compatibility levels: Fully tested · Partially tested · Experimental · Generic · Unsupported. Prune never calls a device fully supported unless its automated tests ran on it. Share this report when you open an issue on GitHub.
App types installed more than once
Phones often ship a manufacturer app and a Google app for the same job. Keep the one you use; the others can usually be disabled. Prune never selects them automatically.
Every app type is installed only once.
Could not open that screen on this phone.
What Prune can do depends on the access you give it
Scan every package, explain it, show usage, open app settings, uninstall apps you installed.
Disable, uninstall-for-user and restore system packages, background restrictions, permissions, battery exemptions, animations, cache trimming.
The same operations through su. Prune does not need root for anything; it is only an alternative to Shizuku.
Free, open-source app by RikkaApps. Lets apps use ADB-level commands without a computer after setup.
Start it in the Shizuku app (see steps below). It must be started again after every reboot.
Shizuku asks you once to allow Prune.
This Shizuku version is too old. Update Shizuku.
Connect to Wi-Fi. In Developer options turn on Wireless debugging (Android 11+; on older versions use the computer method below).
Open Shizuku → Start via Wireless debugging → Pairing. Shizuku shows a notification.
In Wireless debugging, tap Pair device with pairing code. Type the code into Shizuku\'s notification.
In Shizuku tap Start. Then come back here and tap Authorize Prune.
After a reboot, open Shizuku and tap Start again (pairing is remembered).
With a computer instead: enable USB debugging, connect the phone and run the command Shizuku shows under \"Start by connecting to a computer\", usually:
Finds apps you don\'t use, shows screen time and per-app storage. Nothing leaves the phone.
Lets Prune change animation scales directly.

Only if the phone is rooted (Magisk, KernelSU, APatch). Rooting usually needs an unlocked bootloader, can break banking and payment apps, and on Samsung trips Knox permanently. Prune never asks you to root.
Every plan can be exported as an ADB script on the review screen and run from a computer. Prune records it and checks the results afterwards.
Some firmwares (One UI, EMUI, MagicOS) refuse to disable some packages. Uninstall them for this user instead (also reversible).
